<!--
The turnout model's report. It reads only the committed outputs in data/turnout_model/ (no
model fitting here) and writes two files: this page, knitted to docs/turnout-model-2026.html,
and a short summary, docs/turnout-model-2026.md, with its numbers interpolated from the same CSVs.

Run with `make turnout-model` (which runs the four model scripts first), or on its own from the
repo root:

  source("scripts/turnout_model/R/bootstrap.R")
  rmarkdown::render("scripts/turnout_model/report.Rmd", output_dir = "docs",
                    output_file = "turnout-model-2026.html", envir = new.env())

Needs pandoc (RSTUDIO_PANDOC or PATH). Packages: dplyr, tidyr, readr, jsonlite, knitr, ggplot2.
-->

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "", dplyr.summarise.inform = FALSE)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(readr)
  library(jsonlite)
  library(knitr)
  library(ggplot2)
})

# The repo root is two levels above this file, wherever render() is called from.
root <- normalizePath(file.path(dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)), "..", ".."))
p <- function(...) file.path(root, ...)
gg26 <- function(f) p("data/turnout_model/gg26", f)
inp <- function(f) p("data/turnout_model/inputs", f)
rd <- function(f) read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
STATE <- "Maryland"

sw <- rd(gg26("forecast_statewide.csv"))
cty <- rd(gg26("forecast_county.csv"))
lr <- rd(gg26("level_rule.csv"))
lrt <- rd(gg26("level_rule_text.csv"))
bt <- rd(gg26("backtest.csv"))
btc <- rd(gg26("backtest_cells.csv"))
ms <- rd(gg26("mode_split.csv"))
evc <- rd(gg26("early_vote_check.csv"))
sdr <- rd(gg26("same_day_registration.csv"))
cf <- rd(gg26("composition_factors.csv"))
polls <- rd(inp("polls_2026.csv"))
training <- rd(inp("training.csv"))
fit <- fromJSON(gg26("fit_summary.json"))
prov <- function(f) fromJSON(gg26(paste0(f, "_provenance.json")), simplifyVector = FALSE)
p_sw <- prov("forecast_statewide")
p_lr <- prov("level_rule")
p_ms <- prov("mode_split")
p_bt <- prov("backtest")
p_cf <- prov("composition_factors")

stopifnot(nrow(lrt) == 1, all(c("DEM", "REP", "OTH") %in% lr$party_group),
          sum(cty$scenario == "central") == 24, STATE %in% ms$county)

# Formatting. Rates are stored as proportions; ballots as counts.
num <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "", formatC(round(x), format = "d", big.mark = ","))
pct <- function(x, d = 1) ifelse(is.na(x), "", sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f%%"), 100 * x))
pts <- function(x, d = 1) sprintf(paste0("%+.", d, "f"), x)
signed <- function(x) paste0(ifelse(x >= 0, "+", "-"), num(abs(x)))
rng <- function(lo, hi, f = num) paste0(f(lo), " to ", f(hi))
# "a", "a and b", "a, b and c"
join <- function(x) if (length(x) <= 1) paste(x) else paste0(paste(head(x, -1), collapse = ", "), " and ", tail(x, 1))

# One statewide value: scenario x measure x stat (mean, q05, q50, q95).
sv <- function(scenario, measure, stat = "mean") {
  v <- sw[[stat]][sw$scenario == scenario & sw$measure == measure]
  if (length(v) != 1) stop("forecast_statewide.csv has no single row for ", scenario, " / ", measure)
  v
}
party_lab <- c(DEM = "Democrats", REP = "Republicans", OTH = "Other (unaffiliated and minor parties)")
party_short <- c(DEM = "Democrats", REP = "Republicans", OTH = "other voters")
fdate <- function(d, year = TRUE) { d <- as.Date(d); paste0(format(d, "%B "), as.integer(format(d, "%d")), if (year) format(d, ", %Y") else "") }
mail_as_of <- unique(sw$gg26_mail_as_of)

# GG22 eligible registration (active + inactive) is not in the forecast files; it is computed here
# from inputs/inactive_ratio.csv, whose active_gg22 matches training.csv's GG22 active exactly.
inact <- rd(inp("inactive_ratio.csv"))
g22_tr <- training |> filter(election == "GG22") |> group_by(county) |>
  summarise(active = sum(active), ballots = sum(ballots_cast))
g22_el <- inact |> group_by(county) |> summarise(active_ir = sum(active_gg22), eligible = sum(active_gg22 + inactive_gg22)) |>
  inner_join(g22_tr, by = "county") |> mutate(rate_eligible = ballots / eligible)
stopifnot(nrow(g22_el) == 24, all(g22_el$active_ir == g22_el$active),
          sum(g22_el$ballots) == sv("actual_GG22", "ballots"))
gg22_rate_eligible <- sum(g22_el$ballots) / sum(g22_el$eligible)
stopifnot(length(mail_as_of) == 1)
early_as_of <- p_lr$early_as_of
days_out <- lr$days_before_election[1]
```

<p class="note">The forecast uses the State Board of Elections' mail-in figures through
`r fdate(mail_as_of)`, its unofficial early-voting counts through `r fdate(early_as_of$early_voting)`
and its same-day registration counts through `r fdate(early_as_of$same_day_gg26)`. Every number on this page is read from the model's
committed outputs in `data/turnout_model/`. Ballots cast counts every ballot: election day, early
voting, mail-in and provisional. A turnout rate is always ballots cast divided by a named
denominator: active registration, eligible registration (active plus inactive registrants) or
citizen voting-age population (CVAP).</p>

## The forecast in one table

```{r headline-numbers}
c_b <- sv("central", "ballots"); lo_b <- sv("headline_range", "ballots", "q05")
hi_b <- sv("headline_range", "ballots", "q95")
# Invariant of the level rule: central's level lies between the 2022 and 2018 levels.
stopifnot(sv("low", "ballots") <= c_b, c_b <= sv("high", "ballots"), lo_b <= c_b, c_b <= hi_b)
```

The central forecast is `r num(c_b)` ballots cast, `r pct(sv("central", "rate_active"))` of active
registration. The range to quote runs from `r num(lo_b)` to `r num(hi_b)`.

```{r headline-table}
scen <- c(low = "Low (a 2022-like midterm)", central = "Central (the level rule's blend)",
          high = "High (a 2018-like midterm)")
rows <- lapply(names(scen), function(s) tibble(
  Scenario = scen[[s]],
  `Ballots cast` = num(sv(s, "ballots")),
  `90% interval` = paste0(rng(sv(s, "ballots", "q05"), sv(s, "ballots", "q95")), " (within scenario)"),
  `Rate on active` = pct(sv(s, "rate_active")),
  `Rate on eligible` = pct(sv(s, "rate_eligible")),
  `Rate on CVAP` = pct(sv(s, "rate_cvap"))))
hr <- tibble(
  Scenario = "Headline range (low's 5th to high's 95th percentile)",
  `Ballots cast` = paste0("central: ", num(sv("headline_range", "ballots"))),
  `90% interval` = paste0(rng(lo_b, hi_b), " (across scenarios)"),
  `Rate on active` = rng(sv("headline_range", "rate_active", "q05"), sv("headline_range", "rate_active", "q95"), pct),
  `Rate on eligible` = rng(sv("headline_range", "rate_eligible", "q05"), sv("headline_range", "rate_eligible", "q95"), pct),
  `Rate on CVAP` = rng(sv("headline_range", "rate_cvap", "q05"), sv("headline_range", "rate_cvap", "q95"), pct))
act <- lapply(c("GG22", "GG18"), function(e) tibble(
  Scenario = paste0(c(GG22 = "2022 general, actual", GG18 = "2018 general, actual")[[e]]),
  `Ballots cast` = num(sv(paste0("actual_", e), "ballots")),
  `90% interval` = "",
  `Rate on active` = pct(sv(paste0("actual_", e), "rate_active")),
  `Rate on eligible` = if (e == "GG22") pct(gg22_rate_eligible) else "not available",
  `Rate on CVAP` = "not computed"))
kable(bind_rows(rows, list(hr), act), align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
      caption = "Statewide ballots cast and turnout rates. Active = active registration; eligible = active plus inactive registrants (projected for 2026); CVAP = citizen voting-age population (ACS).")
```

Low assumes each party votes at its 2022 statewide level, a quiet midterm. High assumes each party
votes at its 2018 level, an energized midterm. Central blends the two, party by party, with
weights set by the written rule below. The intervals within each scenario are narrow by
construction, because each draw is calibrated to a past election. They carry only cell-level noise
and the shift in the 2026 electorate's mix. The real uncertainty is the spread between low and
high. That is why the headline range runs from low's 5th percentile to high's 95th. The 2022 rate
on eligible divides by that election's active plus inactive registrants, from the board's
inactive counts. No inactive counts exist for 2018, so its rate on eligible is not available. CVAP
comes from a single ACS vintage matched to 2026, so it is not used for the past elections.

The 2026 forecasts include `r num(sdr$extra[sdr$county == STATE])` ballots from same-day
registration beyond 2022's level, the same in every scenario; see
[Ballots already cast](#ballots-already-cast).

The 2026 rate on eligible is projected. There is no 2026 inactive count yet, so eligible is projected
active registration times one plus the average of the 2022 and 2024 inactive-to-active ratios. The
board's own published 2026 percentage will use its actual eligible count and will differ.

## What kind of model this is

The model treats each county and party group as a cell, 72 in all. In each cell, ballots cast are
a binomial share of active registration. The model has three layers. Structure is estimated: how
each cell's turnout sits above or below its party's statewide level in a midterm. Composition is
computed: how the cell's 2026 electorate differs in age and newness from 2022's. Level is set by a
written rule and bracketed between the 2022 and 2018 midterms.

The structure layer is a hierarchical binomial regression, fitted with `lme4::glmer` on
`r fit$n_rows` county x party rows from six elections (2018 and 2022 generals, 2022 and 2026
primaries, 2024 primary and general). It has a free statewide level for each election and party,
four county census covariates, and random effects for county x party, county x election type and
each observation. The formula, from `fit_summary.json`:

```{r formula, results = "asis"}
cat("<pre class=\"rule\">", htmltools::htmlEscape(fit$formula), "</pre>\n", sep = "")
```

```{r varcomp}
vc <- as_tibble(fit$variance_components) |>
  mutate(term = recode(term, obs = "Observation (cell noise)", `county:election_type` = "County x election type",
                       `county:party_group` = "County x party"),
         variance = sprintf("%.4f", variance), sd = sprintf("%.3f", sd))
kable(vc, col.names = c("Random effect", "Variance (logit scale)", "Standard deviation"),
      align = c("l", "r", "r"), caption = "Variance components of the selected fit.")
```

<p class="note">`r fit$selection$why`</p>

## The level rule

```{r rule-numbers}
w <- setNames(lr$w, lr$party_group)
# The sentence below names which votes moved each party's weight; it is built from level_rule.csv.
vote_names <- c(vote_reg = "registration momentum", vote_mail = "mail requests", vote_primary = "primary participation",
                vote_banked = "ballots banked before election day")
moved <- vapply(c("DEM", "REP", "OTH"), function(pp) {
  r <- lr[lr$party_group == pp, ]
  v <- unlist(r[names(vote_names)])
  nz <- v[v != 0]
  if (length(nz) == 0) return(paste0(party_lab[[pp]], ": no index voted, so w stays 0.5"))
  paste0(party_lab[[pp]], ": ", paste0(vote_names[names(nz)], " (", ifelse(nz > 0, "2018-like", "2022-like"), ")",
                                         collapse = " and "), ", so w = ", r$w)
}, character(1))
# Invariant of the rule: every w is bounded to [0.2, 0.8].
stopifnot(all(unlist(lr[c("w", "w_latest", "w_recent")]) >= 0.2 - 1e-9),
          all(unlist(lr[c("w", "w_latest", "w_recent")]) <= 0.8 + 1e-9))
vt <- function(x) ifelse(x > 0, paste0("+", x), as.character(x))
lean <- function(x) ifelse(x < 0.5, "closer to 2022", ifelse(x > 0.5, "closer to 2018", "halfway between 2022 and 2018"))
lean_txt <- join(paste0(party_lab[lr$party_group], " ", lean(lr$w), " (w = ", lr$w, ")"))

# The mail-sensitivity paragraph, generated from level_rule.csv for each alternative projection.
mail_methods <- c(`_latest` = "Holding the latest count", `_recent` = "Extending only the last three snapshots")
# Once a snapshot is dated on or after the request deadline, every projection is the latest count.
after_deadline <- as.Date(mail_as_of) >= as.Date("2026-10-27")
mail_txt <- vapply(names(mail_methods), function(sfx) {
  idx <- lr[[paste0("mail_index", sfx)]]
  lower <- lr$party_group[idx < lr$mail_index]; higher <- lr$party_group[idx > lr$mail_index]
  dir <- if (length(lower) == nrow(lr)) "lower mail indices for every party"
         else if (length(higher) == nrow(lr)) "higher mail indices for every party"
         else paste0(c(if (length(lower)) paste0("lower mail indices for ", join(party_short[lower])),
                       if (length(higher)) paste0(if (length(lower)) "higher ones for " else "higher mail indices for ", join(party_short[higher]))), collapse = " and ")
  if (dir == "") dir <- "the same mail indices"
  v_new <- lr[[paste0("vote_mail", sfx)]]
  ch <- which(v_new != lr$vote_mail)
  votes <- if (length(ch) == 0) "No party's mail vote changes, so every w is unchanged" else
    paste0("The mail vote changes for ", join(paste0(party_short[lr$party_group[ch]], " (", vt(lr$vote_mail[ch]), " to ", vt(v_new[ch]), ")")),
           ", so w becomes ", join(paste0(lr$party_group, " ", lr[[paste0("w", sfx)]])))
  paste0(mail_methods[[sfx]], " gives ", dir, ". ", votes, ".")
}, character(1))
```

The rule puts `r lean_txt`. The weight w is the share of the central level taken from 2018. The
votes that moved it:

`r paste0("- ", moved, ".", collapse = "\n")`

The rule, verbatim from `level_rule_text.csv`:

```{r rule-text, results = "asis"}
rule <- lrt$rule[1]
# Line breaks before each clause for reading; the words are unchanged.
for (k in c(" low:", " high:", " central:", " w_p starts", " Votes, per", " 1\\. ", " 2\\. ", " 3\\. ", " 4\\. ",
            " Amendment:", " Caveat:", " level_rule.csv also")) {
  rule <- gsub(k, paste0("\n", sub("^ ", "", gsub("\\\\", "", k))), rule)
}
cat("<pre class=\"rule\">", htmltools::htmlEscape(rule), "</pre>\n", sep = "")
```

```{r rule-table}
# The momentum caveat, from level_rule.csv: which parties sit outside [-0.5, 1.5].
out <- lr$party_group[lr$reg_position < -0.5 | lr$reg_position > 1.5]
out_txt <- if (length(out) == 0) "No party's momentum position currently lies outside [-0.5, 1.5]." else
  paste0("Registration momentum for ", join(paste0(party_short[out], " (position ", formatC(lr$reg_position[match(out, lr$party_group)], format = "f", digits = 2), ")")),
         if (length(out) == 1) " lies" else " lie", " outside [-0.5, 1.5], beyond the range between 2022 and 2018, so the sign is not interpretable and ",
         if (length(out) == 1) "it casts" else "they cast", " no vote.")
fx <- function(x, d = 3) ifelse(is.na(x), "not used", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d))
lrw <- lr |> select(party_group, everything())
row <- function(label, f) tibble(Quantity = label, !!!setNames(lapply(lrw$party_group, function(pp) f(lrw[lrw$party_group == pp, ])), lrw$party_group))
lrtab <- bind_rows(
  row("Registration momentum, Sept 2025 to Sept 2026", function(r) fx(r$reg_momentum_2026, 4)),
  row("Registration momentum, Sept 2021 to Sept 2022", function(r) fx(r$reg_momentum_2022, 4)),
  row("Registration momentum, Sept 2017 to Sept 2018", function(r) fx(r$reg_momentum_2018, 4)),
  row("Position between 2022 (0) and 2018 (1)", function(r) fx(r$reg_position, 2)),
  row("Vote: registration momentum", function(r) vt(r$vote_reg)),
  row("Mail ballots sent, latest", function(r) num(r$gg26_sent_latest)),
  row(if (after_deadline) "Mail ballots sent, used (latest; sending is over)" else "Mail ballots sent, projected to Oct. 27", function(r) num(r$gg26_sent_projected)),
  row("Mail ballots sent, 2022 final", function(r) num(r$gg22_sent_final)),
  row("Active registration, 2026 (projected)", function(r) num(r$active_2026)),
  row("Active registration, 2022", function(r) num(r$active_gg22)),
  row("Mail sent, raw count ratio 2026/2022", function(r) fx(r$mail_count_ratio)),
  row("Mail sent per registrant, index 2026/2022", function(r) fx(r$mail_index)),
  row("Vote: mail requests", function(r) vt(r$vote_mail)),
  row("Primary ballots, 2026", function(r) num(r$gp26_ballots)),
  row("Primary ballots, 2022", function(r) num(r$gp22_ballots)),
  row("Primary ballots, raw count ratio 2026/2022", function(r) fx(r$primary_count_ratio)),
  row("Primary ballots per registrant, index 2026/2022", function(r) fx(r$primary_index)),
  row("Vote: primary participation", function(r) vt(r$vote_primary)),
  row(paste0("Early votes, 2026 (", days_out, " days out)"), function(r) num(r$gg26_early)),
  row(paste0("Mail ballots received, 2026 (", days_out, " days out)"), function(r) num(r$gg26_mail_received)),
  row("Early votes, 2022", function(r) num(r$gg22_early)),
  row(paste0("Mail ballots received, 2022 (", days_out, " days out)"), function(r) num(r$gg22_mail_received)),
  row("Banked ballots, raw count ratio 2026/2022", function(r) fx(r$banked_count_ratio)),
  row("Banked ballots per registrant, index 2026/2022", function(r) fx(r$banked_index)),
  row("Vote: ballots banked before election day", function(r) vt(r$vote_banked)),
  row("Sum of votes", function(r) vt(r$vote_sum)),
  row("Weight on 2018 (w)", function(r) fx(r$w, 1)))
kable(lrtab, align = c("l", "r", "r", "r"),
      caption = "The level rule's indices, votes and weights by party (level_rule.csv). Momentum is September active registration over the previous September's. OTH has no primary index: Maryland's primaries are closed.")
```

`r if (after_deadline) paste0("**The mail-request deadline has passed.** The board's ", fdate(mail_as_of), " snapshot is dated after the October 27 deadline, so sending is over and every projection uses the latest count of ballots sent. The sensitivities below equal the rule.") else paste("**The mail vote depends on how the mail requests are projected.** The rule extends a straight line through every daily snapshot to the October 27 request deadline.", mail_txt[["_latest"]], mail_txt[["_recent"]])`

```{r mail-sens}
mail_rows <- function(label, sfx) {
  tibble(Projection = label, Party = lr$party_group,
         `Projected sent` = num(lr[[paste0("gg26_sent_projected", sfx)]]),
         `Mail index` = fx(lr[[paste0("mail_index", sfx)]]),
         `Mail vote` = vt(lr[[paste0("vote_mail", sfx)]]),
         `w` = fx(lr[[paste0("w", sfx)]], 1))
}
kable(bind_rows(mail_rows("Rule: line through all snapshots", ""),
                mail_rows("Latest count held", "_latest"),
                mail_rows("Line through last three snapshots", "_recent")),
      align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
      caption = "Mail-projection sensitivity (level_rule.csv _latest and _recent columns).")

ms_sw <- tibble(
  Scenario = c("Central (rule)", "Central, latest mail count held", "Central, last three snapshots"),
  key = c("central", "central_mail_latest", "central_mail_recent")) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(`Ballots cast` = num(sv(key, "ballots")),
         `Difference from central` = if (key == "central") "" else signed(sv(key, "ballots_minus_central")),
         `Rate on active` = pct(sv(key, "rate_active")),
         `Rate on eligible (projected)` = pct(sv(key, "rate_eligible"))) |>
  ungroup() |> select(-key)
kable(ms_sw, align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
      caption = "Statewide central forecast under each mail projection (forecast_statewide.csv).")
```

<p class="note">`r lrt$mail_note[1]`</p>

Caveats on the rule:

- **Mail has no 2018 analogue.** 2018 came before the permanent mail-in list, so the mail index can
  only say whether voters are more or less engaged than in 2022.
- **Banked ballots mix engagement with habit.** Voters have been moving from election day to early
  voting and mail. A voter who voted on election day in 2022 and early in 2026 raises the banked
  index without adding a ballot. The lowest party index is `r sprintf("%.2f", min(lr$banked_index))`
  against the 1.05 threshold, and the vote moves w by one step, like the others.
- **The 2026 primary had an incumbent governor; 2022's was an open seat.** That depresses the
  primary index for reasons unrelated to November. The 2026 primary's party split is also an
  estimate from the voter file.
- **Momentum outside the analogue range votes 0.** `r out_txt`

## Ballots already cast

```{r early-data}
ev <- function(sc, col) evc[[col]][evc$scenario == sc & evc$county == STATE]
stopifnot(all(c("low", "central", "high", "actual_GG22", "actual_GG18") %in% evc$scenario),
          nrow(evc) == 5 * 25, all(table(evc$county) == 5),
          ev("central", "banked") == ms$early[ms$county == STATE] + ms$mail[ms$county == STATE])
lrs <- lr |> summarise(e26 = sum(gg26_early), e22 = sum(gg22_early), m26 = sum(gg26_mail_received),
                       m22 = sum(gg22_mail_received), a26 = sum(active_2026), a22 = sum(active_gg22))
sd_st <- sdr |> filter(county == STATE)
r22 <- ev("actual_GG22", "rate_not_yet_voted"); r18 <- ev("actual_GG18", "rate_not_yet_voted")
where <- function(x) if (x < r22) "below 2022's" else if (x > r18) "above 2018's" else "between 2022's and 2018's"
evc_txt <- paste0("The low scenario needs ", pct(ev("low", "rate_not_yet_voted")), " of them, ", where(ev("low", "rate_not_yet_voted")),
                  " rate; central needs ", pct(ev("central", "rate_not_yet_voted")), ", ", where(ev("central", "rate_not_yet_voted")),
                  "; high needs ", pct(ev("high", "rate_not_yet_voted")), ", ", where(ev("high", "rate_not_yet_voted")), ".")
bv <- setNames(lr$vote_banked, lr$party_group)
banked_vote_txt <- if (all(bv == 1)) "Every party is above 2022 by more than 5%, so every party gets a 2018-like vote" else
  paste0("The vote is ", join(paste0(party_short[names(bv)], " ", vt(bv))))
low_txt <- if (ev("low", "rate_not_yet_voted") < r22) paste0("Read against that, the low scenario asks for less on election day than 2022 delivered (",
  pct(ev("low", "rate_not_yet_voted")), " against ", pct(r22), "), from a pool that has already given up its likeliest voters to early voting and mail.") else
  paste0("The low scenario asks for ", pct(ev("low", "rate_not_yet_voted")), " on election day, against 2022's ", pct(r22), ".")
```

Early voting ended on `r fdate(early_as_of$early_voting, FALSE)`. Voters cast `r num(lrs$e26)` ballots in the eight days, by the
board's unofficial count, against `r num(lrs$e22)` in 2022's certified count, a rise of
`r pct(lrs$e26 / lrs$e22 - 1, 0)` on registration that grew `r pct(lrs$a26 / lrs$a22 - 1, 0)`. By
`r fdate(mail_as_of)`, `r days_out` days before the election, `r num(lrs$m26)` mail ballots had come
back, against `r num(lrs$m22)` at the same point in 2022. The model uses these numbers in three
places:

- **A fourth vote in the level rule.** Early votes plus mail ballots back, per registrant, against
  2022 at the same number of days out:
  `r tolower(substr(banked_vote_txt, 1, 1))``r substr(banked_vote_txt, 2, nchar(banked_vote_txt))` (see the level rule above).
- **The mode split.** Early voting is no longer a forecast: it is the count. Mail is the ballots
  received so far times 2022's late-arrival multiplier, the certified vote-by-mail count over the
  ballots back `r days_out` days before that election, `r sprintf("%.2f", ms$late_multiplier[ms$county == STATE])`
  statewide. Election day is what is left.
- **A check on each scenario.** `r num(ev("central", "banked"))` ballots are already banked or on
  their way: `r num(ev("central", "early"))` early and `r num(ev("central", "mail"))` mail, projected. That leaves
  `r num(ev("central", "not_yet_voted"))` active registrants who have not voted. Each scenario
  implies how many of them must vote on election day or provisionally. In 2022,
  `r pct(r22)` of the registrants who had not voted early or by mail turned out on election day;
  in 2018, `r pct(r18)`. `r evc_txt`

```{r early-table}
lab <- c(low = "2026 low", central = "2026 central", high = "2026 high", actual_GG22 = "2022 actual", actual_GG18 = "2018 actual")
kable(evc |> filter(county == STATE) |> mutate(Scenario = lab[scenario]) |>
        transmute(Scenario, `Ballots cast` = num(ballots), Early = num(early), `Mail-in` = num(mail),
                  `Banked share` = pct(banked_share), `Election day and provisional` = num(election_day_and_provisional),
                  `Registrants not yet voted` = num(not_yet_voted), `Rate among them` = pct(rate_not_yet_voted)),
      align = c("l", rep("r", 7)),
      caption = "Ballots banked before election day and what each scenario needs on November 3 (early_vote_check.csv). 2026 early voting is the board's unofficial count; 2026 mail is projected from ballots received so far. Registrants are active registration.")
```

People who have already voted are the likeliest voters. With a larger share of registrants banked
than in 2022, the ones left are, all else equal, less likely to vote than 2022's were. That makes
this check one-sided: a scenario that needs a higher rate than 2022's from them is asking for more
enthusiasm than in 2022, not just a change of habit. `r low_txt`

**Same-day registration.** During early voting, `r num(sd_st$new26_ev)` people registered and voted
at once, against `r num(sd_st$new22_ev)` in 2022, and `r num(sd_st$addrchg26)` registered voters
updated their address and voted (`r num(sd_st$addrchg22)` in 2022). New registrants are not in the
September-based 2026 registration, so they add ballots the cells cannot see. 2022's same-day
registrants are already in the reference levels, because certified ballots include them, so the
model adds only 2026's excess: election-day same-day registration is projected at 2022's
county counts (`r num(sd_st$new22_ed)` statewide) times the growth in early-voting same-day
registration (`r sprintf("%.2f", sd_st$ev_growth_statewide)`x), for `r num(sd_st$sdr26)` new
registrants in all, against `r num(sd_st$sdr22_scaled)` for 2022 scaled to 2026 registration. The
difference, `r num(sd_st$extra)` ballots, is added to every scenario. Address changes add nothing:
those voters are already on the rolls.

### By county

```{r early-county-data}
# One row per county: central ballots with the low-to-high range, ballots banked, and the
# election-day rate among not-yet-voted registrants each scenario needs, beside 2022 and 2018.
ecw <- evc |> filter(county != STATE) |>
  select(scenario, county, ballots, banked, banked_share, not_yet_voted, rate_not_yet_voted) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = scenario, values_from = c(ballots, rate_not_yet_voted, banked, banked_share, not_yet_voted)) |>
  mutate(gap22 = 100 * (rate_not_yet_voted_central - rate_not_yet_voted_actual_GG22))
# Rows keep early_vote_check.csv's canonical county order.
stopifnot(nrow(ecw) == 24, all(ecw$banked_low == ecw$banked_central), all(ecw$banked_central == ecw$banked_high))
top_gap <- ecw |> slice_max(gap22, n = 3)
# "Less than 2022" only where the gap shows at one decimal place.
below <- ecw |> filter(gap22 <= -0.05) |> arrange(gap22)
n_word <- function(n) c("One", "Two", "Three", "Four", "Five", "Six", "Seven", "Eight", "Nine")[n] %||% as.character(n)
gap_txt <- paste0("The central forecast asks most of ", join(paste0(top_gap$county, " (", pct(top_gap$rate_not_yet_voted_central),
                  " against ", pct(top_gap$rate_not_yet_voted_actual_GG22), " in 2022)")), ".")
below_txt <- if (nrow(below) == 0) "No county's central forecast needs less than its 2022 rate." else
  paste0(if (nrow(below) == 1) "One county's" else paste0(n_word(nrow(below)), " counties'"),
         " central forecast needs less than ", if (nrow(below) == 1) "its" else "their", " 2022 rate: ",
         join(paste0(below$county, " (", pct(below$rate_not_yet_voted_central), " against ",
                     pct(below$rate_not_yet_voted_actual_GG22), ")")), ".")
hi_bank <- ecw |> slice_max(banked_share_central, n = 3)
lo_bank <- ecw |> slice_min(banked_share_central, n = 3)
```

The same check works county by county. Each county's banked ballots are its early-voting count plus
its projected mail; its scenario totals are the forecast's county means. Under the central forecast,
`r join(paste0(hi_bank$county, " (", pct(hi_bank$banked_share_central, 0), ")"))`
have the largest shares of their ballots in before election day, and `r join(paste0(lo_bank$county, " (", pct(lo_bank$banked_share_central, 0), ")"))`
the least. `r gap_txt` `r below_txt`

```{r early-county-table}
kable(ecw |> transmute(
        County = county,
        `Ballots cast, central` = num(ballots_central),
        `Low to high` = rng(ballots_low, ballots_high),
        `Banked` = num(banked_central),
        `Banked share, central` = pct(banked_share_central),
        `Not yet voted` = num(not_yet_voted_central),
        `Needed: low` = pct(rate_not_yet_voted_low),
        `Needed: central` = pct(rate_not_yet_voted_central),
        `Needed: high` = pct(rate_not_yet_voted_high),
        `2022 rate` = pct(rate_not_yet_voted_actual_GG22),
        `2018 rate` = pct(rate_not_yet_voted_actual_GG18)),
      align = c("l", rep("r", 10)),
      caption = "By county: ballots banked before election day (unofficial early-voting count plus projected mail), and the share of active registrants who have not yet voted that each scenario needs on November 3, beside the same rate in 2022 and 2018 (early_vote_check.csv).")
```

## Counties

```{r county-data}
cen <- cty |> filter(scenario == "central")
a22 <- cty |> filter(scenario == "actual_GG22") |> select(county, r22 = rate_active_mean)
a18 <- cty |> filter(scenario == "actual_GG18") |> select(county, r18 = rate_active_mean)
cc <- cen |> left_join(a22, by = "county") |> left_join(a18, by = "county") |>
  left_join(g22_el |> select(county, r22e = rate_eligible), by = "county") |>
  arrange(desc(rate_active_mean))
stopifnot(nrow(cc) == 24, !anyNA(cc$r22), !anyNA(cc$r18), !anyNA(cc$r22e),
          abs(sum(cc$ballots_mean) - c_b) <= 24)
top <- cc$county[1]; bot <- cc$county[24]
n_between <- sum(cc$rate_active_mean >= pmin(cc$r22, cc$r18) & cc$rate_active_mean <= pmax(cc$r22, cc$r18))
# Interval width relative to the forecast, county against statewide.
sw_rel <- (sv("central", "ballots", "q95") - sv("central", "ballots", "q05")) / c_b
n_wider <- sum((cc$ballots_q95 - cc$ballots_q05) / cc$ballots_mean > sw_rel)
```

Central turnout rates on active registration run from `r pct(cc$rate_active_mean[24])` in
`r bot` to `r pct(cc$rate_active_mean[1])` in `r top`. In `r n_between` of 24 counties the central
rate lies between the county's 2022 and 2018 rates. Relative to its forecast, the 90% interval is
wider than the statewide one (`r pct(sw_rel)` of the forecast) in `r n_wider` of 24 counties, because
cell noise averages out across the state.

```{r county-table}
kable(cc |> transmute(County = county, `Ballots cast` = num(ballots_mean),
                      `90% interval (within-scenario)` = rng(ballots_q05, ballots_q95),
                      `Rate on active` = pct(rate_active_mean), `Rate on eligible (projected)` = pct(rate_eligible_mean),
                      `Share of state ballots` = pct(share_of_state_mean),
                      `2022 rate on active` = pct(r22), `2022 rate on eligible` = pct(r22e),
                      `2018 rate on active` = pct(r18)),
      align = c("l", rep("r", 8)),
      caption = "Central scenario by county, sorted by rate on active registration. Active = active registration; eligible = active plus inactive registrants, projected for 2026. 2022 and 2018 rates are actual ballots cast over that election's active registration, or for 2022 also over its active plus inactive registrants.")
```

```{r county-chart, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 7, fig.alt = "Dot-and-range chart of each county's central turnout rate on active registration, with its 90 percent within-scenario interval and the 2022 and 2018 actual rates marked."}
cd <- cc |> mutate(county = factor(county, levels = rev(county)))
marks <- bind_rows(
  cd |> transmute(county, rate = r22, what = "2022 actual"),

marks$what <- factor(marks$what, levels = c("2026 central forecast", "2022 actual", "2018 actual"))
ggplot(cd, aes(y = county)) +

## Who votes: the electorate's party mix

```{r mix-data}
um <- polls |> filter(!is.na(dem_share_lv))
stopifnot(nrow(um) >= 1)
oth_growth <- lr$active_2026[lr$party_group == "OTH"] / lr$active_gg22[lr$party_group == "OTH"] - 1
cmp <- function(a, b, more, less) if (a > b) more else if (a < b) less else "the same"
d_c <- sv("central", "share_DEM"); o_c <- sv("central", "share_OTH"); o_22 <- sv("actual_GG22", "share_OTH")
mix_lead <- paste0("The forecast's electorate is ", cmp(d_c, um$dem_share_lv[1], "more Democratic", "less Democratic"),
                   " than UMBC's likely voters, with ", cmp(o_c, um$una_share_lv[1], "a larger", "a smaller"),
                   " share of other voters.")
oth_txt <- paste0("Other voters cast ", pct(o_c), " of ballots in the central scenario, ",
                  cmp(o_c, o_22, "up from ", "down from "), pct(o_22), " in 2022. Their active registration has ",
                  if (oth_growth >= 0) "grown " else "shrunk ", pct(abs(oth_growth), 0), " since then",
                  if (sign(o_c - o_22) == sign(oth_growth)) ", which drives the change." else ".")
```

`r mix_lead` In the central scenario, Democrats cast `r pct(d_c)` of ballots, against
`r pct(um$dem_share_lv[1], 0)` in UMBC's sample. `r oth_txt`

```{r mix-table}
mix_row <- function(label, s) tibble(Electorate = label, Democrats = pct(sv(s, "share_DEM")),
                                     Republicans = pct(sv(s, "share_REP")),
                                     `Other (unaffiliated and minor)` = pct(sv(s, "share_OTH")))
poll_rows <- um |> transmute(
  Electorate = paste0(pollster, " likely voters, ", fdate(field_start, FALSE), " to ", fdate(field_end), " (n = ", sample_size, ", unweighted)"),
  Democrats = pct(dem_share_lv, 0), Republicans = pct(rep_share_lv, 0),
  `Other (unaffiliated and minor)` = pct(una_share_lv, 0))
kable(bind_rows(mix_row("2026 low", "low"), mix_row("2026 central", "central"), mix_row("2026 high", "high"),
                mix_row("2022 actual", "actual_GG22"), mix_row("2018 actual", "actual_GG18"), poll_rows),
      align = c("l", "r", "r", "r"),
      caption = "Share of ballots cast by party group. Forecast and actual shares use registered party; the poll's shares are as its release reports them.")
```

The forecast's party groups are registered party. A poll's party shares come from its sample,
which may record party as respondents describe it. Many unaffiliated registrants call themselves
Democrats or Republicans when asked. Likely-voter screens also keep the respondents most certain to
vote, and unaffiliated voters are the least likely to say so: UMBC's own enthusiasm figures are lower
for them. UMBC's shares are unweighted by party, so they describe who answered, not the weighted
estimate. The poll is a cross-check here and does not move the forecast.

## Composition

```{r comp-data}
cm <- cf |> filter(county == STATE)
cc_cf <- cf |> filter(county != STATE)
stopifnot(nrow(cc_cf) == 72, nrow(cm) == 3, all(cc_cf$comp > 0))  # the text says comp > 0 everywhere
# The centring constant is the 2026-active-weighted mean of comp per party, recorded by
# 04_forecast.R in forecast_statewide_provenance.json (comp_weighted_mean_removed);
# centred values below are comp minus that constant, computed here from the CSV and JSON.
cmean <- unlist(p_sw$comp_weighted_mean_removed)
# The share of the 2022 electorate missing from today's voter file, from 03_compose.R's provenance.
surv <- p_cf$notes$limitations$factor_age_survivors
held <- as.numeric(sub(".*holds about ([0-9]+)% of the 2022 electorate.*", "\\1", surv))
stopifnot(!is.na(held), held > 50, held < 100)
missing_pct <- 100 - held
d_comp <- sv("central_comp_level", "ballots_minus_central")
d_pts <- 100 * (sv("central_comp_level", "rate_active") - sv("central", "rate_active"))
```

Composition favours turnout in every cell, but the forecast uses it only to shift turnout between
counties. Older electorates and fewer brand-new registrants raise each party's expected 2026 rate.
The statewide level of that boost cannot be trusted, so it is removed.

```{r comp-table}
ord <- c("DEM", "REP", "OTH")
ct <- cm |> mutate(party_group = factor(party_group, ord)) |> arrange(party_group) |>
  left_join(cc_cf |> group_by(party_group) |> summarise(lo = min(comp), hi = max(comp),
                                                         lo_c = county[which.min(comp)], hi_c = county[which.max(comp)]),
            by = c("party_group")) |>
  transmute(Party = as.character(party_group), `Age factor` = sprintf("%+.3f", factor_age),
            `New-registrant factor` = sprintf("%+.3f", factor_new), `Composition (comp)` = sprintf("%+.3f", comp),
            `County range of comp` = paste0(sprintf("%+.3f", lo), " (", lo_c, ") to ", sprintf("%+.3f", hi), " (", hi_c, ")"))
kable(ct, align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "l"),
      caption = "Statewide composition factors by party (logit scale; composition_factors.csv). comp = age factor + new-registrant factor.")

top5 <- cc_cf |> mutate(centred = comp - cmean[party_group]) |> arrange(desc(abs(centred))) |> head(5) |>
  transmute(County = county, Party = party_group, `2026 registrants (voter file)` = num(n26),
            `comp` = sprintf("%+.3f", comp), `comp, centred within party` = sprintf("%+.3f", centred))
kable(top5, align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r"),
      caption = "The five cells whose centred composition factor is largest in size. Centred = comp minus the party's statewide weighted mean (DEM, REP, OTH: see note).")
```

<p class="note">`r lrt$comp_note[1]`</p>

The factors are centred within party for one reason. The 2022 age mix comes from today's voter
file, which lacks the roughly `r missing_pct`% of the 2022 electorate who have since died or moved. That gap is
as large as the factor itself, so its statewide level is not identified. Using the uncentred factor
as a sensitivity adds `r signed(d_comp)` ballots to the central forecast, `r pts(d_pts)` points
on the rate on active registration (`r pct(sv("central_comp_level", "rate_active"))` against
`r pct(sv("central", "rate_active"))`).

## How well the structure predicts a held-out midterm

```{r bt-data}
lose <- p_bt$model_loses_to_naive
act_cty <- training |> filter(election %in% c("GG18", "GG22")) |>
  group_by(election, county) |> summarise(active = sum(active), .groups = "drop")
# County rate errors are computed here from backtest_cells.csv and training.csv's active.
bce <- btc |> group_by(held_out, county) |>
  summarise(actual = sum(actual), predicted = sum(predicted), naive = sum(naive), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(act_cty, by = c("held_out" = "election", "county" = "county")) |>
  mutate(err_model = 100 * (predicted - actual) / active, err_naive = 100 * (naive - actual) / active)
stopifnot(!anyNA(bce$active), nrow(bce) == 48)
n_beat <- sum(bt$model < bt$naive)
mae <- function(h, g, m, col) bt[[col]][bt$held_out == h & bt$grain == g & bt$metric == m]
```

Leaving out one midterm and predicting it from the other elections, the model beats a naive copy
of the other midterm on `r n_beat` of `r nrow(bt)` measures. Its county turnout rates on active registration miss by
`r sprintf("%.1f", mae("GG22", "county", "rate_mae_pts", "model"))` points on average for 2022 and
`r sprintf("%.1f", mae("GG18", "county", "rate_mae_pts", "model"))` for 2018. Both held-out tests calibrate statewide party totals to the actual result, so they test
the county pattern, not the level.

```{r bt-table}
btt <- bt |> mutate(
  `Held-out election` = recode(held_out, GG22 = "2022 general", GG18 = "2018 general"),
  Grain = recode(grain, county = "County", county_party = "County x party"),
  Measure = recode(metric, rate_mae_pts = "Mean abs. error, rate on active (points)",
                   rate_max_abs_pts = "Largest abs. error, rate on active (points)",
                   share_mae_pts = "Mean abs. error, share of state ballots (points)"),
  Model = sprintf("%.2f", model), Naive = sprintf("%.2f", naive),
  Better = ifelse(model < naive, "model", "naive")) |>
  select(`Held-out election`, Grain, Measure, Model, Naive, Better)
kable(btt, align = c("l", "l", "l", "r", "r", "l"),
      caption = "Backtest (backtest.csv). Naive = the other midterm's county x party rate pattern, calibrated the same way.")

worst <- bce |> group_by(held_out) |> slice_max(abs(err_model), n = 3) |> ungroup() |>
  transmute(`Held-out election` = recode(held_out, GG22 = "2022 general", GG18 = "2018 general"),
            County = county, `Actual rate on active` = pct(actual / active),
            `Model error (points)` = pts(err_model), `Naive error (points)` = pts(err_naive))
kable(worst, align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r"),
      caption = "The three counties with the largest model error in each held-out midterm (computed from backtest_cells.csv and training.csv's active registration).")
```

```{r bt-lose, results = "asis"}
lose_txt <- vapply(lose, function(x) {
  m <- recode(x$metric, rate_mae_pts = "mean error in rate", rate_max_abs_pts = "largest error in rate",
              share_mae_pts = "mean error in share of state ballots")
  extra <- if (!is.null(x$worst_model)) paste0(" Both methods miss worst in ", x$worst_model, ".") else ""
  paste0("- Held-out ", recode(x$held_out, GG22 = "2022", GG18 = "2018"), ", ", x$grain, " ", m,
         ": model ", sprintf("%.2f", x$model), ", naive ", sprintf("%.2f", x$naive), " points.", extra)
}, character(1))
cat("The model loses to naive in", length(lose), "places:\n\n")
cat(lose_txt, sep = "\n")
cat("\n")
```

## How the votes will be cast

```{r mode-data}
msw <- ms |> filter(county == STATE)
mcty <- ms |> filter(county != STATE)
stopifnot(nrow(mcty) == 24, sum(mcty$ballots_mean) == msw$ballots_mean,
          msw$mail + msw$early + msw$election_day + msw$provisional == msw$ballots_mean,
          msw$mail + msw$early + msw$election_day + msw$provisional == msw$ballots_mean)
mode_lab <- c(mail = "mail-in", early = "early voting", election_day = "election day", provisional = "provisional")
shares <- unlist(msw[paste0("share_", names(mode_lab))]); names(shares) <- names(mode_lab)
biggest <- names(which.max(shares))
capped <- mcty$county[mcty$mail_capped]
mode_lead <- paste0("Mail ballots make up ", cmp(msw$share_mail, msw$gg22_share_mail, "a larger", "a smaller"),
                    " share of the forecast vote than in 2022, ", pct(msw$share_mail), " against ",
                    pct(msw$gg22_share_mail), ". The largest mode is ", mode_lab[[biggest]], ", at ",
                    pct(shares[[biggest]]), ".")
cap_txt <- if (length(capped) == 0) "No county hit the cap of 90% of its ballots by mail." else
  paste0(join(capped), if (length(capped) == 1) " hit" else " hit", " the cap of 90% of ballots by mail.")
```

`r mode_lead`

```{r mode-sw}
modes <- c(mail = "Mail-in", early = "Early voting", election_day = "Election day", provisional = "Provisional")
kable(tibble(Mode = unname(modes),
             `Ballots cast, 2026 central` = num(unlist(msw[names(modes)])),
             `Share, 2026 central` = pct(unlist(msw[paste0("share_", names(modes))])),
             `Share, 2022 actual` = pct(unlist(msw[paste0("gg22_share_", names(modes))]))) |>
        bind_rows(tibble(Mode = "Total", `Ballots cast, 2026 central` = num(msw$ballots_mean),
                         `Share, 2026 central` = "100.0%", `Share, 2022 actual` = "100.0%")),
      align = c("l", "r", "r", "r"), caption = "Statewide ballots cast by mode, central scenario (mode_split.csv).")
```

Early voting is the board's unofficial count, `r num(msw$early)` statewide; early voting is over.
Mail ballots are the `r num(msw$mail_received)` received by `r fdate(mail_as_of)` times 2022's
late-arrival multiplier in each county (certified vote-by-mail over the ballots back the same number
of days before that election), capped at the ballots sent. That is `r num(msw$mail)` mail ballots,
`r pct(msw$return_rate)` of the `r num(msw$mail_sent)` sent. Provisional ballots keep their 2022
share of each county's vote, and election day is the rest. `r cap_txt`

```{r mode-cty}
kable(mcty |> transmute(County = county, `Ballots cast` = num(ballots_mean), `Mail-in` = num(mail),
                        `Early voting` = num(early), `Election day` = num(election_day),
                        Provisional = num(provisional), `Mail share` = pct(share_mail),
                        `Mail share, 2022` = pct(gg22_share_mail), `Early share` = pct(share_early),
                        `Early share, 2022` = pct(gg22_share_early), `Return rate` = pct(return_rate)),
      align = c("l", rep("r", 10)),
      caption = "Central scenario by county and mode. County ballots are rounded to sum to the statewide total.")
```

## What this cannot see

```{r moore}
gov <- polls |> filter(!is.na(governor_dem), !is.na(dem_share_lv)) |> slice(1)
moore_margin <- round(100 * (gov$governor_dem - gov$governor_rep))
```

- **Election-day weather.** Rain or snow on November 3 would cut election-day voting, forecast at
  `r pct(msw$share_election_day)` of ballots cast.
- **Late changes in the races.** The governor's race polls at Moore +`r moore_margin` (UMBC). A
  tightening race, or a hot down-ballot contest, could lift turnout above the rule's blend.
- **Changes to mail voting.** A court ruling, or a change to a deadline for mail ballots, would
  break the mail projection, which assumes late ballots arrive as they did in 2022.
- **Election-day same-day registration.** It is projected from 2022's county counts and the growth
  in early-voting same-day registration. Other registration after September is not modelled: the
  denominators come from September 2026 active registration.
- **The early-vote count is unofficial.** The certified early-voting count will differ slightly.
- **Survivor bias in composition.** The 2022 age mix is built from today's voter file, which lacks
  people who died or moved since 2022.
- **The 2026 primary's party split is estimated.** The board has not yet published 2026 primary
  turnout by party, so the split comes from the voter file.
- **The 2014 general is left out.** The structure rests on 2018 and later elections.
- **Two different denominators.** The board's 2018 to 2024 turnout sheets divide by active
  registration. Its 2026 guide divides by all eligible voters, active plus inactive. This report
  shows both.

## Data and reproducibility

Run the whole model and this report from the repo root, after `make build-db`:

```
make turnout-model
```

The scripts use the renv project in `scripts/turnout_model/` (`renv.lock`); see
`scripts/turnout_model/README.md`. The forecast reads the board's mail-in files through
`r fdate(mail_as_of)` and its early-voting and same-day files through `r fdate(early_as_of$early_voting)`. Every input and output has a provenance file:

```{r provenance}
pf <- c(list.files(p("data/turnout_model/inputs"), "_provenance\\.json$", full.names = TRUE),
        list.files(p("data/turnout_model/gg26"), "_provenance\\.json$", full.names = TRUE))
ptab <- bind_rows(lapply(pf, function(f) {
  j <- fromJSON(f, simplifyVector = FALSE)
  tibble(File = sub(paste0(root, "/"), "", j$file %||% NA_character_, fixed = TRUE),
         `Provenance file` = sub(paste0(root, "/"), "", f, fixed = TRUE),
         `Made by` = sub("scripts/turnout_model/", "", j$generated_by %||% ""),
         `Run` = substr(j$run_date %||% "", 1, 10))
}))
ptab <- bind_rows(ptab, tibble(File = "data/turnout_model/gg26/fit_summary.json",
                               `Provenance file` = "(self-describing)", `Made by` = "02_fit.R",
                               Run = substr(fit$run_date, 1, 10)))
stopifnot(!anyNA(ptab$File), all(ptab$Run != ""))
kable(ptab, caption = "Model inputs and outputs, each with its provenance file and run date.")
```

```{r summary-md}
# The short summary, written from the same numbers. Each figure is interpolated from the CSVs.
s_line <- function(s, label) {
  paste0("- **", label, ":** ", num(sv(s, "ballots")), " ballots cast (within-scenario 90% interval ",
         rng(sv(s, "ballots", "q05"), sv(s, "ballots", "q95")), "); ",
         pct(sv(s, "rate_active")), " of active registration, ", pct(sv(s, "rate_eligible")),
         " of eligible registration (active plus inactive, projected).")
}
cty_line <- function(d) paste0(d$county, " ", pct(d$rate_active_mean), collapse = "; ")
md <- c(
  "# Maryland 2026 general election turnout forecast",
  "",
  paste0("Mail-in data through ", fdate(mail_as_of), "; early voting and same-day registration through ",
         fdate(early_as_of$early_voting), ". Generated by `scripts/turnout_model/report.Rmd`; the full report is `docs/turnout-model-2026.html`."),
  "",
  "## Statewide ballots cast",
  "",
  s_line("low", "Low (a 2022-like midterm)"),
  s_line("central", "Central (the level rule's blend)"),
  s_line("high", "High (a 2018-like midterm)"),
  "",
  paste0("The range to quote is ", rng(lo_b, hi_b), " ballots cast (low's 5th to high's 95th percentile), ",
         rng(sv("headline_range", "rate_active", "q05"), sv("headline_range", "rate_active", "q95"), pct),
         " of active registration. For comparison, ", num(sv("actual_GG22", "ballots")), " ballots were cast in 2022 (",
         pct(sv("actual_GG22", "rate_active")), " of active registration, ", pct(gg22_rate_eligible),
         " of eligible registration) and ", num(sv("actual_GG18", "ballots")),
         " in 2018 (", pct(sv("actual_GG18", "rate_active")), ")."),
  "",
  "## Ballots already cast",
  "",
  paste0(num(ev("central", "early")), " early votes (unofficial, voting over) and ", num(lrs$m26),
         " mail ballots received by ", fdate(mail_as_of), ", projected to ", num(ev("central", "mail")),
         " mail ballots in all: ", num(ev("central", "banked")), " ballots banked before election day, ",
         pct(ev("central", "banked") / ev("actual_GG22", "banked") - 1, 0), " more than 2022's ",
         num(ev("actual_GG22", "banked")), ". The central forecast needs ", pct(ev("central", "rate_not_yet_voted")),
         " of the registrants who have not yet voted to vote on November 3 (2022: ", pct(r22), "; 2018: ", pct(r18), "). ",
         "Same-day registration beyond 2022's level adds ", num(sd_st$extra), " ballots to every scenario."),
  "",
  "## Party mix of the electorate",
  "",
  paste0("Central scenario: Democrats ", pct(sv("central", "share_DEM")), ", Republicans ",
         pct(sv("central", "share_REP")), ", other ", pct(sv("central", "share_OTH")),
         " of ballots cast, by registered party. ", um$pollster[1], " likely voters (unweighted): Democrats ",
         pct(um$dem_share_lv[1], 0), ", Republicans ", pct(um$rep_share_lv[1], 0), ", other ",
         pct(um$una_share_lv[1], 0), "."),
  "",
  "## Counties (central rate on active registration)",
  "",
  paste0("- Highest: ", cty_line(head(cc, 5)), "."),
  paste0("- Lowest: ", cty_line(tail(cc, 5)[5:1, ]), "."),
  "",
  "## Counties against the ballots already cast",
  "",
  "Central ballots cast (low to high), ballots banked before election day, and the share of registrants who have not yet voted that the central forecast needs on November 3, against the same rate in 2022.",
  "",
  "| County | Central | Low to high | Banked | Needed, central | 2022 rate |",
  "|---|---|---|---|---|---|",
  paste0("| ", ecw$county, " | ", num(ecw$ballots_central), " | ", rng(ecw$ballots_low, ecw$ballots_high), " | ",
         num(ecw$banked_central), " | ", pct(ecw$rate_not_yet_voted_central), " | ",
         pct(ecw$rate_not_yet_voted_actual_GG22), " |"),
  "",
  "## Caveats",
  "",
  "- The spread between scenarios is the real uncertainty; within-scenario intervals are narrow by construction.",
  "- The central weights come from a written rule; the mail and banked-ballot indices have no 2018 analogue, and the banked index counts voters who moved from election day to early voting as engagement.",
  "- The early-voting count is the board's unofficial tally; late mail is projected at 2022's rate of arrival.",
  "- The 2026 primary had an incumbent governor, and its party split is estimated from the voter file.",
  "- Composition is centred within party because the voter file lacks the 2022 voters who died or moved.",
  "- Not modelled: election-day weather, late changes in the races, changes to mail-voting rules, registration after September other than same-day registration.",
  "- The 2014 general is left out.",
  "- The board's 2018-2024 sheets divide by active registration; its 2026 guide divides by all eligible voters. Both are shown."
)
writeLines(md, p("docs", "turnout-model-2026.md"))
```
